mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5% signals rising inflation that may prompt monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% and UNRATE monthly change < -0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by >0.5% and UNRATE decreases by >0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST declines by >0.5% in the late-cycle regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rise above 0.5% signals imminent monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 0.5% and RSAFS monthly change > 0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by >0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime, a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE declines by >0.1% in the high-unemployment regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
